profile.headline: Software Engineer at Facebook | Co-Founder of SacHacks
profile.summary:
I've always had a knack for learning.

It started when I was 7 years old and wanted to learn an instrument. But of course, I could not pick just one; I picked three. It started with the piano, expanded to the drums, and culminated at the clarinet. By this point, I could be a one-woman band.  

After learning all the music theory, it was time to get physical…by joining the marching band! Those were some of the best years of my life--performing music for large crowds while being one of many players forming shapes on the field.

Once it was time to choose my college major, I took a shot in the dark with Computer Science and I loved it! Once again, I could not pick just software or hardware; I wanted to learn both. After all, the possibilities of interfacing them together are endless!

After learning strong fundamentals in software and hardware, I took on roles to contribute to my college community. There, I found my passion for leadership. I then realized I wanted to be a technical leader throughout my career, so I completed a Technology Management minor. After all, being able to look at a problem through both a developers’ and business leaders’ viewpoint was a lethal combination that I wanted to have. 

At this point, I had learned a tremendous amount but wanted to provide others the foundation to learn as well. That is when I co-founded SacHacks, Sacramento’s first major intercollegiate hackathon. The idea came about when I realized that our state's capital hadn’t provided its students the opportunity to meet on a large scale and create projects that could change the world. Also, students did not have the financial means to gain access to and learn about up and coming technologies. Now, this just would not do; so, I brought it all to them. At SacHacks, students from all over the globe could work with VR/AR, Blockchain, Machine Learning, and even develop on a Tesla! 

Once I graduated from college, I became involved in and learned every stage of the software development cycle at Texas Instruments. Then, I challenged the status quo by automating test framework generations, optimizing legacy code, and organizing the site’s first holiday celebration in 15 years. 

Now, I am onto the next big learning opportunity: learning about you! Let’s connect and continue to learn together.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Server Integrity Team - Storage Hardware Infrastructure

• Implement Identity Enrollment Verification to prevent malicious hardware attacks and authenticate hardware cryptographic identities for 4.8 million hosts
• Develop a centralized key management and firmware signing service named Sirius to function as a source of truth for cryptographic keys and be the official signing service for all ASICs
• Improve Attestation reliability and decrease fallback frequency by replaying the kernel’s register value via event logs rather than filesystem artifacts

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Tape HAL Team - Storage Hardware Infrastructure

• Improve data durability by extending HAL functionality to enable Dynamic Braking validation
• Increase Headnode Service reliability by adding system error handling to prevent crash looping when a drive disappears
• Discover and resolve an overestimate in shutdown timeouts that delayed updates by 64 times
• Accumulate crash information in stored drive dumps to maintain and debug drives at scale

positions.title: Co-Founder
positions.description:
• Spearhead Sacramento’s first major intercollegiate hackathon with 350 hackers in attendance
• Acquire a partnership with the Sacramento Kings resulting in a $5,000 sponsorship, a national press release, 3 prize tracks, the Chief Technology Officer Ryan Montoya being a keynote speaker, and 3 judges from the Kings' team
• Secure a dual-title sponsorship with the McClellan Conference Center and associated XYO Blockchain company to provide a venue and associated costs worth $40,000
• Recruit and lead a cross-functional team of 40 across engineering, design, operations, and finance
• Achieve Major League Hacking (MLH) Member Event status for the 2019 hackathon season resulting in $1,000 from GitHub, a listing on the MLH Season Schedule, and hardware and software labs for the hackers
• Attain MLH's Finish Line Fund Grant worth $1,000 to improve hacker experience

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Reduce code size by 20% by optimizing low-level device drivers to maximize code reuse
• Develop a UART driver in C with DMA functionality for two microcontroller product families
• Create and automate UART driver tests for full coverage of software requirements
• Drive multiple international teams to improve functional requirement test traceability by 33%
• Decrease manual maintenance time by 80% by optimizing the automated test framework to utilize a JavaScript-based file generation tool (SysConfig)
• Engage with customers to identify, implement, and verify resolutions for software defects
• Utilize Agile Lifecycle Management and Software Configuration Management tools including JIRA, Confluence, Jenkins, Git, and Bitbucket
• Organize virtual events to bolster team morale due to the transition to remote work as of March 2020

positions.title: Virtual Reality Lead
positions.description:
• Invent a VR Center to provide students access to equipment such as Oculus Rift and HTC Vive
• Develop product development workshops to teach entrepreneurs Unity and ProBuilder
• Provide students with VR opportunities and resources that would otherwise be unattainable

positions.description:

projects.title: Sound Localization Autonomous Recording Unit
projects.description:
• Acquire data from the microphones in order to make a servomotor point to the direction of sound
• Construct an amplifying circuit in a soldered protoboard
• Develop a virtual instrument in LabVIEW to calculate the angle detected
• Design a user interface to offer 6 recording features including timed, triggered, and stereo.

projects.title: Canvas Calendar Converter
projects.description:
• Build a Chrome Extension during HackDavis 2018 to curate Google Calendar events based on Canvas courses
• Develop JavaScript code to parse Canvas data to interface with the Google Calendar REST API
